item.title: Universal and Reciprocating Domains in Classes of Continua and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2611.11671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the notions of reciprocating domains in classes of topological spaces. A reciprocating domain is a member of a class that maps onto every member which maps onto it. We provide general characterizations, showing in particular that in upward directed classes reciprocating domains coincide with universal domains. We investigate these domains in several classes of compact metrizable spaces and continua. We also construct a chainable universal domain admitting a continuous monotone surjection onto a pseudoarc although every nondegenerate subcontinuum of the domain contains an arc. In particular, a chainable reciprocating domain need not contain a pseudoarc.
item.dc:creator: Iztok Bani\v{c}, Goran Erceg, Judy Kennedy, Chris Mouron, Van Nall

item.title: Topological Lifting of Mundici Equivalence and Di Nola--Lettieri Equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2611.10087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that summability characterises precisely when a topological MV-algebra can be realized as the unit interval of a lattice-ordered topological abelian group, thereby providing a topological lifting of both Mundici equivalence and DiNola--Lettieri equivalence. Applications include a Birkhoff--Kakutani-type metrisation theorem, a second-countability criterion, and a topological extension of a key continuity lemma from the proof theory of first-order {\L}ukasiewicz logic---following Baaz--Metcalfe's hypersequent approach to approximate completenesss---and provides an $A$-valued topological semantics for the approximate strong completeness of~$\mathbf{G}\text{{\L}}\forall$, where $A$ ranges over summable topological MV-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Jia, Yichuan Yang

item.title: A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.10850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.
item.dc:creator: Arash Pourkia

item.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu

item.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.10935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.
item.dc:creator: Dirk Hofmann, Rui Prezado

item.title: Weak $\lambda$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mr\'owka spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.11025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $\lambda$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $\lambda$-space is a $\lambda$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $\omega_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $\lambda$-set is a $\lambda$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>\omega_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Ismael Corral Rojas, Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues, Victor dos Santos Ronchim

item.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.12365v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $\sigma$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.
item.dc:creator: C\"uneyt \c{C}evik

item.title: Rationally Null-homologous Floer Simple Knot
item.description: arXiv:2611.12522v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every rationally null-homologous Floer simple knot in a closed, oriented, irreducible three-manifold with nonzero Thurston norm is unknotted. The proof combines a cut-and-reglue comparison for extremal Floer groups with Binns's theorem on Floer-minimal knots in balanced sutured manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Zhaojun Chen

item.title: Function spaces, web spaces, and Lawson-compactness in Domain Theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.11671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the structural properties of function spaces and their connections with Lawson-compactness and web spaces in domain theory. First, using finite-refinement and palette methods, we characterize the topological spaces $X$ for which the function space $[X\to L]$ is an RB-domain for every RB-domain $L$. In particular, we establish the equivalence between this preservation property and the condition that $X$ is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space. We further investigate its relationship with RW$^*$-spaces and obtain partial results concerning the Lawson-Mislove's problem. Second, we construct a countably based topological space $Z$ that is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space, but is neither a wide web space nor a C-space. More precisely, its lattice of open sets is a continuous frame satisfying $\kappa$-distributivity for every finite cardinal $\kappa\geq 2$, while failing to be $\omega$-distributive. This provides a negative answer to a question raised by Erne and demonstrates that finite distributivity, even at every finite level, does not imply countable distributivity. Finally, by introducing labelled posets and employing constructions based on presheaves over finite sets and their element posets, we prove that every Lawson-compact domain is a Scott-continuous retract of a Lawson-compact algebraic domain, thereby answering a problem proposed by Kou. As applications, we show that the function space from an RB-domain to a Lawson-compact domain is Lawson-compact. Moreover, for an FS-domain $X$, we establish that $X$ is an RB-domain if and only if $[X\to L]$ is Lawson-compact for every Lawson-compact domain $L$. This characterization also yields the existence of an FS-domain $X$ and a Lawson-compact algebraic domain $L$ for which $[X\to L]$ is not continuous. This gives a negative answer to the question raised by Shen et al.
item.dc:creator: Wei Luan, Qingguo Li

item.title: A New Approach to Universal Measurability
item.description: arXiv:2609.14414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: V. Fedorchuk, A. Chigogidze and T. Banakh in 2003 and V. Bogachev in 2024 posed the following questions: (i) is it true that $P_\tau(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_\sigma(X)$; (ii) is it true that $P_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_R(\beta X)$ if and only if $X$ is pseudocompact, where $P_\sigma$, $P_\tau$ and $P_R$ are the functors of probability measures on the space $X$ that are, respectively, $\sigma$-additive on the Baire $\sigma$-algebra, $\tau$-additive, and Radon? The answers to these questions are negative. In this paper the questions are put into a general framework: for spaces of measures $Q_p(X)\subset Q_q(X)$ of various types we study when $Q_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $Q_q(X)$. It is proved that for spaces of alternating measures $M_p(X)\subset M_q(X)$ the $C$-embeddedness, the $C^*$-embeddedness and the $G_\delta$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and a criterion in terms of sequences of continuous functions is given. The question of $C$-embedding of measure spaces is an extension of the question of coincidence of measure spaces, which is a development of the classical concepts of universally measurable and universal measure zero sets. Note (corrected version): incorrect statements of the previous versions are marked or removed; see the last section of the paper.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: E. A. Reznichenko and Yu V. Sadovnichiy. A new approach to universal measurement. Bulletin of the Institute of Mathematics of the National Academy of Sciences of the Kyrgyz Republic, (2):2, 2025
item.dc:creator: Reznichenko E. A., Sadovnichiy Yu. V

item.title: $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-networks, $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizability, and local HCP-finiteness
item.description: arXiv:2609.30317v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every admissible ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, we prove that every regular space with a $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving (HCP) $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-metrizable, answering Problem~5.2 of Zhou--Liu--Liu--Lin. The proof combines existing characterizations with a local countability bound. If $y_n\to_{\mathcal{I}} x$ in a space $X$ and $\{n:y_n\ne x\}\in\mathcal{I}^{+}$, then every point-discrete family of $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is countable. If no such sequence exists at $x$, then $\{x\}$ itself is an $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhood. These alternatives imply that every space with a $\sigma$-point-discrete $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal{I}$-$snf$-countable. We say that $\mathcal{I}$ has local HCP-finiteness if, in every $T_1$ space, the convergence and support assumptions above imply that each HCP family of $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is finite. A countable Rudin--Keisler antichain of free ultrafilters gives an admissible ideal without this property, so the countability bound cannot in general be strengthened to finiteness. Every $P^{-}$ ideal has local HCP-finiteness. We give sufficient conditions for Fubini products, heterogeneous Fubini sums, and increasing unions to preserve this property. These results establish local HCP-finiteness for the finite Fubini powers of $\mathrm{Fin}$, Kat\v{e}tov's first limit-stage ideal $\mathrm{Fin}^\omega$ and its finite successors, the tree-derived rank-$\omega$ ideal $\mathcal H_{<\omega}$, and the inductive-limit ideal $\mathrm{Fin}_\omega$. All these examples except $\mathrm{Fin}$ fail $P^{-}$.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
item.description: arXiv:2610.02212v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\theta$ be an ordinal and let $(N_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $\rho G$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_\alpha=\overline{N_\alpha}^{\rho G}$ and $H_\alpha=GK_\alpha$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_\alpha$ mark the first stages at which points of $\rho G$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $\theta$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,\theta]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $\delta<\theta$ the successive factor $N_{\delta+1}/N_\delta$ is compact exactly when $\delta+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:\rho G\to\rho(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{\rho G}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $\rho G\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $\rho N\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(\rho G)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $\rho G\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $\rho N$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.13973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We show that it need not be, even when the space is hereditarily precompact. On the integers, take the distance of an irrational rotation and add a fixed toll $c>0$ to every step from a nonnegative integer down to a smaller one. The resulting space, the toll spiral, is a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, and the shift $n\mapsto n+1$ is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction works over any metric space $Y$: for every bijective isometry $\sigma$ of $Y$ and every point whose $\sigma$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, adding the same toll along the orbit gives such a counterexample, for instance over the $p$-adic odometer. The conjugate of the toll spiral is not even precompact, so the hypothesis on the conjugate in Zavarzina's positive result cannot be dropped, even for bijections. The toll spiral is also not expand-contract plastic, since the inverse shift is a non-expansive bijection that is not an isometry. For an arbitrary bijective non-contractive map $F$, the distance from $F^kx$ to $F^ky$ has a limit as $k\to-\infty$; $F$ is an isometry for this limit, and the excess $D_0$ of the distance over it is the defect. On a hereditarily precompact space, we prove a monochromy theorem: if a pair $(a,b)$ has positive defect $\eta$, then there are natural numbers $t_1<t_2<\cdots$ such that either $D_0(a,F^{-\Delta}a)>\eta/4$ for every difference $\Delta=t_j-t_i$ with $i<j$, or $D_0(F^{-\Delta}b,b)>\eta/4$ for every such $\Delta$. Three boundary results delimit the remaining question; the open case, that of separated spaces compact in one of their topologies, has since been settled by the author (arXiv:2610.14301). The construction, in general and for the circle, is machine-checked in Lean 4 using Mathlib, with no unproved steps.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Duzer

item.title: Uniformization of topological MV-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.01779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, First, we prove that for every topological MV-algebra the topology is induced by a uniformity. As a application, we obtain that every topological MV-algebra is completely regular and every \(T_0\) first countable topological MV-algebra is metrizable. Second, we study the completion of the canonical difference uniformity in topological MV-algebra. Finally, we construct some examples show that not all topological MV-algebras are canonically completable and the property of canonically completable topological MV-algebra does not imply local order convexity.
item.dc:creator: Li-Hong Xie, Jiang Yang

item.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.10930v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pr\"ahauser
